title: Finite surjective detection of potentiality of fixed pinnings
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $f:T\to S$ be a finite surjective morphism between Noetherian excellent schemes with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-exc-excellent-ring]. Fix a dimension function $\delta_S$ and set $\delta_T(t)=\delta_S(f(t))$. Use ordinary small-etale $D^+$ and the exceptional right adjoint $f^!$ to $f_*=Rf_!$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Suppose $K\in D^+(S_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ has pointwise pinnings
$$p_s:R\Gamma_sK\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(\delta_S(s))[2\delta_S(s)]$$
with the costalk convention of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]; compatibility with residue transitions is not assumed. At $t\mapsto s$, let $a_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the residue-field morphism [def-weil-residue-field], and equip $f^!K$ with the pinning $(a_t^*p_s)\circ\beta_{f,t,K}^{-1}$, where $\beta$ is the specified Gysin-normalized costalk comparison of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] (relative transcendence degree zero). For finite $f$ these $\beta$-induced pinnings coincide with the induced putative pinnings of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection], defined there through $R\Gamma_t(f^!K)\cong\pi^!R\Gamma_sK$ and the inverse finite-field Gysin isomorphism $\operatorname{Cl}_\pi$ of the residue extension $\pi=a_t$: both comparisons are the canonical supported identification followed by the Gysin class of the finite residue-field extension, which is the canonical etale identification for a separable extension and multiplication by the degree for a purely inseparable one. Consequently, by the finite-surjective clause of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection], the original pinnings make $K$ potential if and only if these induced pinnings make $f^!K$ potential, in the sense of the residue-transition compatibility of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. The content of this node beyond that lemma is the agreement of the two normalizations of the induced pinnings.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.3, with the induced putative pinnings of Proposition 2.4.3.1 and composition normalization of Remark 2.4.3.2, pp. 266-267

proof.text: A finite morphism is proper and has finite fibres by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Thus $f$ is separated, finite type and quasi-finite, and has the compactification $T\xrightarrow{1}T\xrightarrow fS$. Fix $t\mapsto s$, and put $k=\kappa(s)$, $L=\kappa(t)$, $a=a_t$, $N=C_sK$, and $d=\delta_S(s)$. On an affine neighbourhood of $s$, finiteness means a module-finite algebra by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; tensoring a finite list of module generators with $k$ shows that the fibre algebra is finite-dimensional over $k$. Its prime quotients are finite-dimensional domains, hence fields: multiplication by a nonzero element is injective and therefore surjective. Consequently all fibre points are closed, $L/k$ is finite, and the reduced closure of $t$ in the fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Its regular nonempty open in the recipe of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] is therefore this whole point, and the relative transcendence degree is zero. The supported comparison of [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus] is the canonical isomorphism $c:C_t(f^!K)\xrightarrow{\sim}a^!N$. These reductions use no compatibility of the pinnings.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.1 proof and Lemma 4.4.1; finite-morphism geometry is Stacks Tags 01WN and 02NU

proof.text: Write $\operatorname{Cl}^{\mathrm{reg}}_a$ and $\operatorname{Cl}_a$ for the virtual-dimension-zero classes $\Lambda_L\to a^!\Lambda_k$ of [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin] and of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity] (the class in the putative formula of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection]). They agree. Factor $a$ as a regular closed immersion $i:\operatorname{Spec}L\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^m_k$ of codimension $m$ followed by the projection $p$. By its statement, $\operatorname{Cl}^{\mathrm{reg}}_a$ composes the product of codimension-one Kummer classes of a regular sequence for $i$ with the orientation of $p$ of [lem-trf-ambient-diagonal-purity-base-change]. The absolute class is constructed, for this factorization, as the composite of the supported Kummer class $\eta_i$ of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus], which is that flag product with the sign $+c_1$, and the orientation of [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality]. This is the construction in the proof of absolute purity; its statement says only `canonical'. The two smooth orientations are the same specified map: diagonal restriction, deformation to the zero section of $T_{P/k}$, and inverse Kummer-normalized vector-bundle purity. Any residual sign convention $\pm1$ per Kummer factor would multiply by $\varepsilon^m$; replacing $i$ by $\operatorname{Spec}L\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{m+1}_k$ changes $m$ by one. Both classes are factorization-independent, so $\varepsilon=1$.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1 and the following paragraph (quasi-finite agreement); Proposition 2.4.3.1; XVI, Theorem 2.5.12 and Corollary 3.1.2

proof.text:
For $Q\in D^+(k_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ set
$$G_a(Q)=T_a(\Lambda,Q)\circ(\operatorname{Cl}_a\otimes1_{a^*Q}):a^*Q\longrightarrow a^!Q.$$
The class and the tensor map are isomorphisms, the latter by [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor]. The finite-field instance of the specified construction of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-gysin] is exactly
$$\beta_{f,t,K}=c^{-1}\circ G_a(N).$$
Indeed its regular open is $\operatorname{Spec}L$, so there is no remaining generic restriction, and its regular-closed/smooth composite is the displayed class extended to $N$ by the counit-defined tensor map: the composition identity $T_{kh}=h^!T_k\circ T_h(k^!,k^*)$ of [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor] turns the closed-immersion and smooth comparisons into $T_a(\Lambda,N)\circ(\operatorname{Cl}^{\mathrm{reg}}_a\otimes1)$, and $\operatorname{Cl}^{\mathrm{reg}}_a=\operatorname{Cl}_a$ by Step 2. The same supported-composition identification $c$ occurs in the putative construction. For $A=\Lambda_k(d)[2d]$, $G_a(A)$ is precisely the twisted finite-field Gysin map $\operatorname{Cl}_a$ used there.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1 and the following paragraph (quasi-finite agreement); Proposition 2.4.3.1; XVI, Theorem 2.5.12 and Corollary 3.1.2

proof.text:
Apply naturality of $T_a$ from [lem-per-field-exceptional-tensor] to the given pinning $p_s:N\xrightarrow{\sim}A$. Since $\operatorname{Cl}_a$ is fixed and tensor is functorial, this gives the equality of actual maps
$$a^!(p_s)\circ G_a(N)=G_a(A)\circ a^*(p_s).$$
Invert $G_a(N)$ and $G_a(A)$ and compose with $c$. Using Step 3, the pinning specified in the item becomes
$$a^*(p_s)\circ\beta_{f,t,K}^{-1}
 =a^*(p_s)\circ G_a(N)^{-1}\circ c
 =G_a(A)^{-1}\circ a^!(p_s)\circ c.$$
The last expression is exactly the pinning displayed in [lem-per-putative-finite-detection]. Its target is $\Lambda_L(d)[2d]$, because $\delta_T(t)=d$ and pullback identifies the signed roots-of-unity twist over $k$ with that over $L$. Thus equality holds for the fixed pinnings at every point, before any residue-compatibility condition is imposed.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 4.4.1, paragraph identifying its quasi-finite pinnings with Proposition 2.4.3.1; explicit naturality calculation

proof.text: Check the two normalizations mentioned in the statement. If $L/k$ is separable, [lem-exc-etale-coproduct-etale] with a singleton index makes $a$ etale. It is smooth of relative dimension zero. Its orientation is the smooth orientation of [lem-per-noetherian-prime-power-smooth-duality], which by Step 2 is also the smooth clause of [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin]. At relative dimension zero that orientation and its coefficient extension are the etale adjunction comparisons. Hence both constructions give the canonical etale comparison in this case. If $L/k$ is purely inseparable in characteristic $p\ne\ell$, the last clause of [lem-per-prime-power-regular-gysin] instead identifies $\operatorname{Cl}_a$ with multiplication by $[L:k]$ under the tautological etale equivalence. By the formula for $G_a$ in Step 3 the same scalar occurs before taking the inverse in each induced pinning; in particular both contain the inverse degree factor, rather than silently discarding it. The degree is a unit as asserted by that lemma. These checks verify the stated normalizations; Step 4 already treats arbitrary finite residue extensions without a separability assumption.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 2.4.3.3 proof (purely inseparable degree); Lemma 4.4.1; XVI, smooth Gysin normalization

proof.text: The coefficients, bounded-below ordinary etale category, excellence, invertibility of $\ell$, and dimension function are exactly those of [lem-per-putative-finite-detection]. Our $f$ is finite and surjective, and the given pointwise pinnings make $K$ putative without any initial residue compatibility. That lemma supplies the dimension function $\delta_T=\delta_S\circ f$ and says that $K$ is potential if and only if $f^!K$ with its putative induced pinnings is potential. Substitute the pointwise equality of pinnings proved in Step 4. The residue-compatibility squares are now literally the same squares, with the same maps and twist-shifts, so this equivalence is exactly the one requested for the $\beta$-induced pinnings.
